baseline_fixed_column.question: what ro_carboxylate reports, and what it is looking at when it says there is none

refused_offset_calls.rule: an offset window call is accepted only if the type's curated reference carries the SAME carboxylate at column 431
refused_offset_calls.why: measured: at the exact column Asp:Glu is 130:1, in the offset window 1.25:1 -- an offset reading picks up any nearby carboxylate instead of the ligand

baseline_fixed_column.note: window_entirely_gapped = the column and its neighbours are GAPS IN THE ALIGNMENT; there is NO residue there to read, so this is an alignment event. substituted_residue_in_place = a real residue sits at the column but it is not a carboxylate; this is a biological claim. offset_call_unsupported_by_reference = the window found a carboxylate at an offset but the reference does not confirm it; the reading was refused and fell through to the anchored reading.

mechanism.question: whether the carboxylate column (431) falls inside the region of the entry that aligned at all
mechanism.anchor_note: The Parales/Gibson consensus D-x(2)-H-x(3-5)-H (Complete_thesis.pdf, sec. 3.1, citation [104]) is intact in every one of these entries. The D in that consensus is the BRIDGING aspartate (column 286), not the facial-triad carboxylate (column 431); so the consensus does not locate the carboxylate, it confirms that the anchor is sound.

window_widening.question: whether widening the fixed column in MODEL coordinates brings the carboxylate back
window_widening.note: If the column is a GAP in the alignment then widening only scans more gaps. An entry this step cannot recover is one that a simple register shift does not explain.

naive_anchor.question: whether a D/E sits in a RAW distance window calibrated against His-2
naive_anchor.verdict: The window is 95 residues wide and the chance expectation is 99.5%; this reading is NOT evidence ON ITS OWN, it needs the anchored reading of step 6.

reference_profile_probe.question: whether sub-models built from the references can reach the catalytic lobe of these sequences at all

models.why: the Rieske [2Fe-2S] domain -- POSITIVE CONTROL, it must hit in every set
the C-terminal catalytic lobe -- the region the carboxylate column lies in
the carboxylate surroundings only -- a narrow, sensitive local probe

reference_profile_probe.control_note: rieske_only = candidates with 'the Rieske centre intact, the catalytic triad rejected'; the pipeline does NOT count these as RO alpha. A probe that also fails on this control shows NOT that the carboxylate-less set are not ROs, but that the probe cannot reach that region.

anchored_reread.question: whether the carboxylate is there when it is read anchored to the positives of the same type rather than at a FIXED column
anchored_reread.method: re-alignment per type with mafft --auto; the carboxylate column is the mode of the positives' known carboxylate positions in the RAW sequence; members without a carboxylate are read at that column within a window of +-3 columns
anchored_reread.reproducibility: mafft was run single-threaded: this output is reproducible byte for byte.

by_ncbi_product_annotation.question: NCBI'nin 'SRPBCC family protein' / 'Rieske 2Fe-2S domain-containing protein' gibi etiketleri, katalitik merkezin yokluguna isaret ediyor mu

residue_offset_from_expected.definition: the RAW distance from the carboxylate found to His-2, minus the median distance in that type's positives. A shift relative to the fixed column is undefined for these entries, because the column is a gap in the alignment; so the shift is measured against the EXPECTED DISTANCE instead.
residue_offset_from_expected.how_to_read_this: The register test is in offset_distribution: a 0 there says the carboxylate is at the SAME alignment column as the positives, that is, in the homologous position. The residue-distance deviation here measures something DIFFERENT: how much indel has accumulated in the ~140-residue stretch between the His pair and the carboxylate. A wide deviation does not show an error, it shows WHY THE FIXED COLUMN SLIPS -- the insertions and deletions in that stretch shift the model's register.

null_model.test: per type: the number of D/E observed at the anchor column against that group's OWN tail D/E frequency, a one-sided binomial, corrected with Benjamini-Hochberg
null_model.comparison: the D/E fraction of every column in the same alignment that is at least 80 % occupied is also reported (median_column_DE_fraction); if the anchor column sits inside that distribution there is no signal

real_absences.question: what the entries that still have no carboxylate after the anchored reading actually are

c_terminal_reach.question: whether the protein reaches as far as the place the carboxylate would sit
c_terminal_reach.note: protein_ends_before_the_expected_site = for these entries 'no carboxylate' is not a SUBSTITUTION, it is the sequence ending.

clustering.reading: if the number of leaves is close to the number of entries they are scattered; if they pile into one leaf they are a single divergent clade

components_hmm.limitation: This library holds NO model for the CATALYTIC domain of the ring-hydroxylating alpha subunit (PF00848 / Ring_hydroxyl_A are not in it) and Pfam-A is not available locally; so an output of 'the Rieske domain only' SAYS NOTHING on its own about the architecture. SRPBCC (PF03364/PF10604, the helix-grip fold) cannot be tested either -- the NCBI product strings are reported as they are under by_product.

residual_family_scan.question: whether the residual entries, aligned AMONG THEMSELVES, carry a conserved carboxylate column anchored to His-2
residual_family_scan.why: The anchor of step 6 rests on the type's BACTERIAL positives; if the carboxylate has moved to a family-specific, non-homologous position that anchor cannot see it. If every member of a family carries a D/E at the same column then the carboxylate IS there, only somewhere the reference set cannot reach.

verdict.headline: Of the 3408 entries that appear to have no carboxylate, 3377 (99.1 %) are an ARTEFACT OF THE FIXED COLUMN: read anchored to the positives of the same type, the carboxylate is in place. The real absence is 24 entries (0.7 %).
verdict.why_the_fixed_column_failed: 2280 of the missing calls (66.9 %) come from the column ITSELF and its neighbours being GAPS in the alignment; in only 239 does a real residue that is not a carboxylate sit at the column. The cause is not a shift of one or two positions: in 1858 of these entries (54.5 %) the ROmotif71 alignment NEVER REACHES the carboxylate column -- the median last filled match column is 415, while the carboxylate column is 431. Model coverage averages 0.71 (against 0.84 in the set with a carboxylate) and the hmm score 279 (against 399). So the 426-column reference model cannot align the C-terminal catalytic lobe of these sequences; the column falls OUTSIDE the region that aligned. The reference-profile probe shows this directly: the C-terminal catalytic lobe model (ROcatC, columns 260-426) scores >=20 in only 64.4 % of these sequences, against 93.6 % in the set with a carboxylate and 0.6 % in the 'Rieske present, catalytic rejected' control set that the pipeline does NOT count as RO. The narrow carboxylate probe (ROcarbox, columns 330-380) reaches 0.0 % in the carboxylate-less set and 21.5 % in the set with one. The Rieske-domain probe, by contrast, holds near 100 % in ALL THREE sets -- so what is lost is not the Rieske centre, it is the reference model's REACH into the catalytic lobe.
verdict.why_this_is_not_a_window_problem: Widening the same fixed column out to +-40 columns recovers only 69.0 % of them -- widening over gaps only scans more gaps.
verdict.why_the_naive_anchor_was_not_enough: The window is 95 residues wide and the chance expectation is 99.5%; this reading is NOT evidence ON ITS OWN, it needs the anchored reading of step 6.
verdict.what_the_anchored_reading_did: In every type the members without a carboxylate were re-aligned with mafft together with the members OF THE SAME TYPE whose carboxylate is known and with the curated reference sequence; the carboxylate column was then decided by the vote of the positives' known positions rather than by a fixed number. The method's own accuracy was measured in the same alignment: in a median 100.0 % of the positives the anchor returned the right residue. The shift distribution piles up ON the anchor (column shift 0: 3112 entries; deviation from the expected His-2 distance within +-3 residues: 819 / 3376), so what is being read is not a random D/E but the carboxylate in the HOMOLOGOUS position. This passes a binomial test against the group's own D/E composition in 39 of 45 types.
verdict.what_the_real_absences_appear_to_be: 24 entries, scattered over 11 types; the residues sitting at the anchor column are {'-': 22, 'S': 1, 'N': 1}. 22 of those are a gap at that column in the alignment, so even their 'absence' may still come from the limit of the measurement. They sit in 17 different leaves, so they are NOT a single divergent clade but a scattered residue. The domain-architecture test cannot draw a distinction because the component_hmms library holds no model for the catalytic domain of the ring-hydroxylating alpha subunit. C-terminal reach: {'long_enough_to_hold_the_site': 11, 'protein_ends_before_the_expected_site': 11, 'site_falls_in_the_last_20_residues': 2}. The WITHIN-FAMILY last check: when the residual entries are aligned among themselves, 0 of them carry a conserved carboxylate at a family-SPECIFIC position (none); so they have a carboxylate too, only somewhere the 71 bacterial references cannot reach. The remaining 24 entries cannot be resolved by this method because they are eukaryotic Rieske oxygenase subfamilies represented once or twice (pheophorbide a oxygenase, chlorophyllide a oxygenase, PTC52/TIC55, cholesterol 7-desaturase/daf-36): what is left is not a set of FALSE POSITIVES but a GAP IN THE REFERENCE SET.
verdict.what_about_the_SRPBCC_annotation: The NCBI product strings are not evidence that these entries are NOT oxygenases: the anchored reading found the catalytic carboxylate in place in 231 of the 231 entries labelled 'SRPBCC family protein' (100.0 %); 1189 of the 1200 entries labelled 'Rieske 2Fe-2S domain-containing protein' (99.1 %); 34 of the 35 entries labelled 'hypothetical protein' (97.1 %). Those labels are partial CDD calls that land on one piece of the protein only; next to that piece sits a complete mononuclear iron centre.
verdict.are_they_Rieske_oxygenases: Yes, the evidence points that way. In EVERY member of the set that appears to lack a carboxylate, 4/4 of the Rieske ligands, both catalytic histidines and the bridging Asp/Glu are in place -- that is, the D-x(2)-H-x(3-5)-H consensus the thesis reports is intact. On the anchored reading the facial triad's carboxylate was found as well, in 99.1 % of them. These entries look far from being ROs for a reason that is not biological but methodological: the reference set consists of 71 BACTERIAL ring-hydroxylating types, while 341 of this group are eukaryotic (Rieske oxygenases of the chlorophyll and steroid pathways: pheophorbide a oxygenase, TIC55, chlorophyllide a oxygenase, cholesterol 7-desaturase), and their catalytic lobe cannot be aligned to a bacterial model.
verdict.should_the_admission_rule_change: NO, it should not be tightened to 3/3. On the fixed-column reading a 3/3 rule would cost 3408 entries (16.2 %) and lose members in 46 types; but that number is INFLATED, because almost all of the loss is not a real biological absence, it is the model's reach. On the anchored reading the real cost is 31 entries (0.15 %). So a 3/3 rule would throw 3377 genuine ROs that DO have the carboxylate out of the database, and the types it would hit hardest (3_321_Nvd, 7_701_AerC, 6_602_CAO, 1_108_PobA) are the ones furthest from a curated reference, that is, the most valuable. The 2/3 choice in ro_motif.py is CONFIRMED by this measurement.
verdict.what_should_change_instead: The MEASUREMENT should change, not the rule. (1) ro_carboxylate's catalytic_residue and catalytic_offset fields should carry the fact that they were read at a fixed column: a NULL offset means 'could not be read in the window', not 'absent', and today the table does NOT make that distinction. (2) For entries with low coverage the carboxylate should be written from the within-type anchored reading. (3) UPDATE 2026-10-30: this item used to say that the reference set held NO eukaryotic RO type. It now does -- 6_601_PAO, 6_602_CAO and 6_603_PTC52 were added on 14 October 2026 and recruit 617 members; Nvd and DAF-36 are in the set as well. EVEN SO most of the remaining real absences are still in those types (PTC52, CAO, DAF36, Nvd), so the problem is not the ABSENCE of a reference but that the catalytic lobe of these subfamilies does not align to a bacterial profile: the fix is not to add references, it is to anchor the column within the type.
